places.name: Porto
places.summary: Portugal's second city, stacked on granite hills above the Douro. Compact historic centre, tiled churches, port lodges across the river and a strong food scene; the obvious base for the north.
facts: Centre is walkable but very hilly; wear good shoes
Driving and parking in the old centre is hard; use garages or metro
Metro line E links the airport to the centre in ~30 min
Many sights are within 15 min walk of Avenida dos Aliados
places.season: Mild but rainy October–April; pack a rain jacket.

places.name: Ribeira riverfront
places.wiki: Historic Centre of Oporto, Luiz I Bridge and Monastery of Serra do Pilar
places.summary: The UNESCO-listed riverside quarter of narrow lanes and colourful tall houses facing the Douro and Gaia's port lodges. The classic Porto scene, lively day and night.
facts: Touristy restaurants on the quay; better value a street or two back
Lovely at sunset and after dark
Steep stairways connect it to the Sé and upper town

places.name: Dom Luís I Bridge
places.summary: Two-deck iron arch bridge (1886) linking Porto and Vila Nova de Gaia. Walk the upper deck, shared with the metro, for the best views of Ribeira and the river.
facts: Upper deck reached from the Sé side or Jardim do Morro in Gaia
Lower deck links Ribeira quay with the Gaia cellars
Watch for trams on the upper deck: walk on the side paths

places.name: Livraria Lello
places.summary: Neo-Gothic bookshop (1906) with a carved wooden interior and famous red forked staircase. Gorgeous but very crowded; worth it if you book a timed slot.
facts: Timed tickets online; ~€10, deductible from a book purchase
First slot of the day is the least crowded
Queues outside can be long without a booking

places.name: Clérigos Tower
places.summary: Baroque church and 75 m bell tower by Nicolau Nasoni, Porto's skyline symbol. About 240 steps lead to a 360° view over the old town and river.
facts: Buy tickets online to skip the line

places.name: Porto Cathedral (Sé)
places.summary: Fortress-like Romanesque cathedral on the highest point of the old town, with a Gothic cloister lined in azulejos. The terrace in front looks over the Ribeira roofs.
facts: Terrace and viewpoint free at any hour
Next to the upper deck of Dom Luís I Bridge
Combine with Ribeira on the walk down

places.name: São Bento Station
places.summary: Working railway station whose entrance hall is covered with some 20,000 blue-and-white azulejo tiles showing Portuguese history. Quick and free.
facts: Trains to Guimarães, Braga and up the Douro to Pinhão leave here
Busy at rush hour; early morning is calmer

places.name: Palácio da Bolsa
places.summary: 19th-century stock exchange palace, visited by guided tour only. The highlight is the gilded Moorish-revival Arab Room.
facts: Tours run in several languages; buy at the door or online
Next to Ribeira and São Francisco Church

places.name: Serralves Museum & Park
places.summary: Contemporary art museum by Álvaro Siza set in 18 ha of gardens with an Art Deco villa, woodland and a treetop walk. A calm half day away from the centre.
facts: Combined museum + park ~€25; park-only ticket cheaper
Allow 2–3 h; park is best in dry weather
Bus from the centre or ~15 min taxi

places.name: Casa da Música
places.summary: Rem Koolhaas's angular concert hall at Rotunda da Boavista. Take a guided tour or, better, catch a concert.
facts: Guided tours most days; book ahead
Metro Casa da Música station alongside

places.name: Foz do Douro
places.summary: Upmarket district where the Douro meets the Atlantic, with a seafront promenade, lighthouses on the breakwater and small rocky beaches. Good for a sunset walk.
facts: Historic tram line 1 runs from Ribeira along the river
Seafood restaurants and cafés along the front
Waves often crash over the Felgueiras pier
places.caution: Stay off the breakwater in big swells; waves sweep over it.

places.name: Matosinhos
places.summary: Port town just north of Porto with a long sandy beach and a street of charcoal grills famous for fresh fish. Go for a grilled-fish lunch and a walk on the beach.
facts: Metro line A from the centre (~25 min)
Rua Heróis de França is the grilled-fish street
places.season: Beach is for walks Oct–May; Atlantic water ~15–17 °C even in summer.

places.name: Port wine cellars (Vila Nova de Gaia)
places.summary: Across the river from Ribeira, dozens of port houses (Taylor's, Graham's, Sandeman, Cálem, Ferreira…) age their wine in lodges and offer tours with tastings.
facts: Book a timed tour in high season
Graham's and Taylor's are uphill but have river views
Cable car (Teleférico de Gaia) links the quay with Jardim do Morro

places.name: Bolhão Market
places.summary: Porto's historic two-level food market, reopened in 2022 after restoration. Fish, produce, cheese and small food stalls in a 19th-century iron-and-stone hall.
facts: Good for picnic supplies and a quick lunch

places.name: Six Bridges river cruise
places.summary: Short cruise in a traditional rabelo-style boat from Ribeira or Gaia, passing under Porto's six Douro bridges. Easy way to see the city from the water.
facts: Sit on the open deck for photos
places.season: Can be cancelled when the river is high after heavy winter rain.

places.name: Jardim do Morro & Serra do Pilar
places.summary: Park and terrace on the Gaia end of Dom Luís I Bridge, below the Serra do Pilar monastery. The best panorama of Porto, especially at sunset.
facts: Metro Jardim do Morro stop on line D
Very busy at sunset; arrive early
Cable car runs down to the Gaia cellars

places.name: Braga
places.summary: Lively university city and Portugal's religious capital, full of baroque churches. Pleasant old centre and gateway to Bom Jesus and Peneda-Gerês.
facts: Underground car parks around the centre
Good base for day trips to Guimarães and Gerês

places.name: Braga Cathedral (Sé)
places.summary: Portugal's oldest cathedral, begun in the 11th century, mixing Romanesque, Gothic and baroque. The treasury and chapels hold rich sacred art.
facts: In the heart of the old town

places.name: Bom Jesus do Monte
places.summary: UNESCO-listed hilltop sanctuary above Braga reached by a monumental zigzag baroque stairway. Ride the 1882 water-powered funicular up and walk the stairs down.
facts: Wooded park with lake behind the church

places.name: Guimarães
places.summary: 'Birthplace of Portugal', with a beautifully preserved UNESCO medieval centre around Largo da Oliveira. Great atmosphere in the evenings.
facts: ~1 h 15 min by train from Porto
Old town is pedestrian; park outside
Cable car up to Penha hill
Easy to combine with Braga in a day

places.name: Guimarães Castle
places.summary: 10th-century keep and walls on the hill associated with Afonso Henriques, first king of Portugal. Small but symbolic, with views over the town.
facts: ~€2; combined ticket with the Ducal Palace available

places.name: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
places.wiki: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
places.summary: 15th-century palace with striking brick chimneys, heavily restored in the 20th century. Rooms show tapestries, furniture and fine wooden ceilings.

places.name: Ponte de Lima
places.summary: One of Portugal's oldest towns, on the Lima river with a long medieval and Roman bridge. Calm, green and known for vinho verde and rural manor guesthouses.
facts: Fortnightly Monday market on the riverbank
Good base for the Lima valley and Soajo

places.name: Viana do Castelo
places.summary: Elegant coastal town at the mouth of the Lima, with a Renaissance main square, filigree gold and traditional costume heritage. Ocean beaches across the river.
facts: Gil Eannes hospital ship museum in the harbour
Big Senhora da Agonia festival in August
Good base for the northern coast and Valença

places.name: Santa Luzia Sanctuary
places.summary: Neo-Byzantine basilica on Monte de Santa Luzia above Viana. Climbing the dome gives one of Portugal's great views over the Lima estuary and coast.
facts: Basilica free; small fee for the dome
Funicular from town (~€3 return) or drive up
Narrow final stairs in the dome
Clear days best for the view

places.name: Valença Fortress
places.summary: Star-shaped 17th-century fortress town on the Minho river facing Tui in Spain. Ramparts with views, and lanes full of linen and towel shops.
facts: Walk across the old iron bridge to Tui
Busy with Spanish shoppers at weekends

places.name: Barcelos
places.summary: Market town that gave Portugal its rooster symbol. Best on Thursday for one of the country's largest weekly markets, plus a medieval bridge and pottery museum.
facts: Thursday market on Campo da República
Easy stop between Braga and the coast

places.name: Gerês (Caldas do Gerês)
places.summary: Old spa village in a deep valley inside Peneda-Gerês National Park, with hotels and guesthouses. The practical base for the park's waterfalls, viewpoints and trails.
facts: Limited services Nov–Mar; book accommodation ahead
Petrol and groceries are scarce in the park; fill up in Braga
places.season: Cool and wet in winter; waterfalls fullest late autumn to spring.

places.name: Pedra Bela viewpoint
places.summary: Rocky viewpoint above Gerês village looking over the Caniçada reservoir and the Gerês valley. Short drive up a forest road.
facts: Continue on to Cascata do Arado
Morning or late afternoon light best

places.name: Arado Waterfall
places.summary: Waterfall dropping down granite slabs in the heart of the park, with a viewing platform a short walk from the road near Ermida.
facts: Combine with Pedra Bela on the same road
Mountain road is narrow and partly rough
places.season: Most water from late autumn to spring; thin in late summer.

places.name: Tahiti Waterfall (Fecha de Barjas)
places.summary: Series of cascades and turquoise pools on the Arado river near Ermida. One of the park's most photographed spots.
facts: Steep, slippery path down from the road
places.caution: Rocks are very slippery and people have died here; do not climb or jump into the pools.

places.name: Portela do Homem Waterfall
places.summary: Waterfall and clear pools right by the road near the Spanish border, reached through the Mata da Albergaria oak forest. A Roman road (Geira) with milestones runs nearby.
facts: Short walk from the border road
Albergaria forest road has stopping restrictions in summer
Combine with the Geira Roman milestones

places.name: Soajo
places.summary: Granite mountain village in the Peneda part of the park, famous for its cluster of stone espigueiros (raised granaries) on a rock outcrop.
facts: Quiet rural tourism houses for overnight

places.name: Lindoso
places.summary: Village near the Spanish border with a small restored castle beside a field of some 50 granite espigueiros. A striking, photogenic combination.
facts: Castle has a small fee and limited hours

places.name: Sistelo
places.summary: Remote village in the Vez valley surrounded by terraced fields, nicknamed 'the little Portuguese Tibet'. A short riverside walk links its terraces and bridges.
facts: Riverside walking trail along the Vez
Little to eat out of season

places.name: Peso da Régua
places.summary: Riverside town at the western gateway of the Douro wine region, terminus of many river cruises. Home to the Douro Museum and plenty of hotels.
facts: Train from Porto São Bento ~2 h
Practical base with more services than Pinhão
Scenic N222 runs east to Pinhão

places.name: Pinhão
places.summary: Small village in the heart of the port vineyards, surrounded by terraced quintas. The railway station has fine azulejo panels of harvest scenes.
facts: Train from Porto ~2 h 30 min along the river
Book accommodation early in harvest season (Sept)
places.season: Harvest in September; vines turn red and gold in late October.

places.name: Quinta wine tastings around Pinhão
places.summary: Wine estates around Pinhão (e.g. Quinta do Bomfim, Quinta da Roêda, Quinta do Seixo, Quinta do Crasto further west) offer cellar tours and port and Douro wine tastings with valley views.
facts: Book ahead, especially weekends and harvest
Choose a driver or book a tour: roads are steep and winding
Some quintas close or reduce hours in winter

places.name: São Leonardo de Galafura viewpoint
places.summary: High chapel viewpoint above Régua with a sweeping view over the river's curves and the vineyard terraces. Celebrated by writer Miguel Torga.

places.name: Casal de Loivos viewpoint
places.summary: Viewpoint high above Pinhão looking straight down on a bend of the Douro and its terraced slopes. Often called the finest view in the valley.
facts: Steep narrow road up from Pinhão
Small parking area at the miradouro
places.caution: Very steep, narrow road with tight bends; take it slowly.

places.name: Lamego
places.summary: Historic bishops' town south of Régua, known for sparkling wine and its baroque Nossa Senhora dos Remédios sanctuary. Cathedral and museum in the centre.
facts: Good base on the quieter south bank

places.name: Nossa Senhora dos Remédios Sanctuary
places.summary: Baroque pilgrimage church at the top of a grand zigzag stairway of nearly 700 steps decorated with azulejos and statues. Views over Lamego.
facts: You can drive to the top and walk down
Big pilgrimage festival in late August/September

places.name: Mateus Palace
places.summary: Baroque manor near Vila Real, famous from the Mateus Rosé label. Visit the furnished rooms and formal gardens with a cedar tunnel and reflecting pool.

places.name: Amarante
places.summary: Pretty riverside town on the Tâmega with an arched granite bridge and the São Gonçalo church and convent. Known for its convent pastries.
facts: About 45 min from Porto on the A4
Try doces conventuais at Confeitaria da Ponte
Good stop between Porto and the Douro

places.name: Douro river cruise (Pinhão)
places.summary: Boat trips from Pinhão (1–2 h) through the terraced vineyard landscape; longer day cruises run from Porto or Régua with return by train or coach.
facts: Sit outside on the upper deck
places.season: Fewer departures November–March; full-day cruises mostly run April–October.

places.name: Côa Museum
places.wiki: Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley and Siega Verde
places.summary: Striking concrete museum above the confluence of the Côa and Douro, explaining the valley's Palaeolithic rock engravings. Good introduction before visiting the open-air sites.
facts: Book rock-art site tours in advance (museum website)
Near Vila Nova de Foz Côa

places.name: Côa Valley rock art (Penascosa)
places.wiki: Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley and Siega Verde
places.summary: UNESCO-listed open-air Palaeolithic engravings of horses, aurochs and ibex, seen on guided 4x4 tours. Penascosa leaves from Castelo Melhor; night visits also possible.
facts: Hot in summer, cold on winter evenings

places.name: Miranda do Douro
places.summary: Border town on the cliffs above the Douro gorge, with a cathedral and its own language, Mirandese. Known for posta mirandesa beef steak.
facts: Spanish border dam crossing next to town
Combine with the Douro International boat

places.name: Douro International gorge boat trip
places.summary: Boat trip into the deep granite canyon of the Douro on the Portuguese–Spanish border, with high cliffs and nesting griffon vultures.
places.season: Reduced schedule in winter; check before travelling.

places.name: Bragança
places.summary: Remote capital of Trás-os-Montes, crowned by a walled medieval citadel. Base for the Montesinho Natural Park and its schist villages.
facts: ~2 h 30 min from Porto by motorway
Hearty regional food: alheira, roast kid

places.name: Bragança Citadel
places.summary: Walled village with a 15th-century castle keep, the unusual civic Domus Municipalis and a stone pillory. Small military museum inside the keep.

places.name: Montesinho Natural Park
places.summary: Remote upland park of oak and chestnut woods and traditional schist-and-granite villages, home to wolves and deer. Montesinho village is a good walking start.
places.season: Chestnut colours in late October/November; snow possible in winter.

places.name: Rio de Onor
places.summary: Communal village straddling the Spanish border, half Portuguese and half Spanish, with stone houses along a stream. A glimpse of old Trás-os-Montes life.

places.name: Chaves
places.summary: Spa town on the Tâmega with a Roman bridge, a medieval keep and a museum built over Roman baths. Known for its smoked ham and pastéis de Chaves.
facts: Roman baths museum (Museu das Termas Romanas) small fee
Easy motorway link (A24) to Vila Real and Régua
